name: [v2.5.0] Token revocation, sandbox network policies & SQL over Hub datasets
body:
## 🚨 Revoke leaked tokens with `hf auth revoke`

If a token ever leaks — committed to a repo, pasted in a log, shared in a snippet — you can now revoke it right away with `hf auth revoke`. Revocation doesn't require being logged in: anyone holding the raw value of a token can revoke it, and the token owner gets notified by email. To rule out footguns, the request is deliberately sent without your own `Authorization` header, so your active token can never be revoked by mistake. The same is available in Python with the new top-level `revoke_tokens()` helper, which sends tokens in batches of 1000. Note that the Hub always answers with a generic "revocation requested" message, whether the token existed or not.

```bash
>>> hf auth revoke hf_xxx hf_yyy
✓ Revocation requested for 2 token(s)
  count: 2
```

```python
>>> from huggingface_hub import revoke_tokens
>>> revoke_tokens(["hf_xxx"])
```

📚 **Documentation:** [`hf auth revoke` in the CLI guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/main/en/guides/cli) · [`revoke_tokens()` reference](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/main/en/package_reference/authentication)

- [CLI] Add `hf auth revoke` to revoke leaked tokens by @Wauplin in #5389

## 🌐 Sandbox network policies: no internet access, or an allowlist

Sandboxes can now run without internet access, or with access restricted to an allowlist. Pass `network="none"` to block all outbound connections, or `network={"allow": [...]}` with IP ranges, IPs (optionally with a port) and hostnames — for example, to let an agent in a sandbox reach your internal vLLM server and the Hub, and nothing else. The policy is enforced by the sandbox server with seccomp and Landlock, applies to every process the sandbox starts, and cannot be removed from inside the sandbox, even by root. Pools support it per-sandbox too, so one host can run isolated and connected sandboxes side by side. If the server cannot apply the policy (e.g. a pool host started by an older version of `huggingface_hub`), creation fails with a `SandboxError` instead of silently returning a connected sandbox.

```python
sbx = Sandbox.create("python:3.12", network="none")  # volumes still work
sbx = Sandbox.create("python:3.12", network={"allow": ["10.0.0.0/8", "203.0.113.10:443", "huggingface.co"]})
agent = pool.create(network="none")  # pools can mix isolated and connected sandboxes
```

```bash
hf sandbox create --network none
hf sandbox create --network 10.0.0.0/8,huggingface.co:443
```

📚 **Documentation:** [Sandboxes guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/main/en/guides/sandbox)

- [Sandbox] Add network policies: no internet access, or an allowlist by @Wauplin in #5303

## 🦆 Query datasets with `hf_dataset()` in `hf datasets sql`

`hf datasets sql` now auto-installs and loads the Hugging Face DuckDB extension, so you can query a dataset with `hf_dataset('org/name')` instead of hand-building `read_parquet(...)` URLs against the Dataset Viewer. This is a nice ergonomics win for agents previewing datasets, and as a side effect it also enables writing back to the Hub with `COPY ... TO 'hf://datasets/username/dataset-name/...'`. The extension requires DuckDB 2.0+; if it cannot be installed (older DuckDB or an unsupported platform), a warning is logged and existing `read_parquet` workflows keep working unchanged.

```bash
>>> hf datasets sql "SELECT * FROM hf_dataset('stanfordnlp/imdb') LIMIT 3"
```

📚 **Documentation:** [`hf datasets sql` in the CLI guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/main/en/guides/cli)

- Support hf_dataset() in `hf datasets sql` by @lhoestq in #5371

## 💾 fsspec transactions for buckets

`HfFileSystem` now supports [fsspec transactions](https://filesystem-spec.readthedocs.io/en/latest/features.html#transactions) for buckets. Files written inside a `fs.transaction` block are uploaded when the block ends, and nothing is uploaded if the block raises. This unlocks libraries that wrap every save in a transaction, such as PyTorch Lightning's `_atomic_save`, which previously could not write checkpoints to `hf://buckets/...` paths. Transactions are best-effort (each file is uploaded separately on commit, so a failure can leave earlier files uploaded) and buckets-only: repo writes, `rm` and `cp_file` inside a transaction raise a `NotImplementedError` before any upload or delete.

```python
>>> with hffs.transaction:
...     with hffs.open("buckets/my-username/my-bucket/checkpoints/last.ckpt", "wb") as f:
...         f.write(data)
...     # not uploaded yet
>>> # uploaded now
```

📚 **Documentation:** [Transactions in the HfFileSystem guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/main/en/guides/hf_file_system)

- [HfFileSystem] Support fsspec transactions for buckets by @davanstrien in #5272
- [Docs] Document HfFileSystem transactions for buckets by @davanstrien in #5332

## 🔐 Spaces OAuth without a client secret (PKCE)

`OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` is now optional when adding Hugging Face OAuth to a Space. PKCE (S256) is always enabled: without a secret, the Space authenticates as a public OAuth client (`token_endpoint_auth_method="none"`), while Spaces that still receive a client secret keep working as before. Session cookies are now signed with a key derived from `SPACE_SIGNING_SECRET` — a stable per-Space secret injected by the Hub — instead of `OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, so sessions survive restarts and are shared across replicas, and secretless Spaces no longer share a predictable cookie key. Heads-up: the signing key changes with this release, so users logged in to an OAuth Space will need to log in again once the Space upgrades `huggingface_hub`.

- Make OAuth client secret optional for Spaces (PKCE support) by @moon-bot-app[bot] in #4578

## 🤖 Chat completions routed through the Hub router

When calling `chat_completion` with a Hugging Face token and a specific `provider`, requests now go through the Hub router at `/v1/chat/completions` with `model` set to `hf-model-id:provider`, instead of calling provider-specific routes directly. Provider routes skip the router's server-side routing (`auto`, `:cheapest`/`:fastest`/`:preferred` policies, model pinning), so pinned-provider calls now follow exactly the same path as `auto` calls and the Hub code snippets, with OpenRouter picking a serving provider and failing over automatically if one is down or rate limited. Calls with a provider API key are unchanged and still reach the provider directly, and the chat provider helpers dropped by this change are no longer needed by the client.

📚 **Documentation:** [Inference guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/main/en/guides/inference)

- [Inference Providers] Route chat through the router and drop chat provider helpers by @hanouticelina in #5333
